 This appeal coming on for admission this day, Justice Su
 Arvind Dharmadhikari passed the following:
 Order
Heard on the question of admission and interim relief.

2. The instant intra-court appeal preferred under Section 2(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Uchcha Nyayalaya(Khand Nyaypeeth Ko Appeal) Adhiniyam, 2005 assails the final order passed by the learned Single Judge dated 09.02.2023 in W.P. No.4212/2017 dismissing the petition in question by which challenge was made to the rejection of candidature of petitioner for appointment to the post of Constable(Driver) in Police Force on the ground that the petitioner had antecedents of Crime No.33/2012 registered at Police Station Begumganj, District Raisen for the offences punishable under Sections 363, in alternate Section 363/120-B, 366 in alternative Section 366/120-B, 366-A and 376(2)
(f)/120-B of IPC, out of which the petitioner was acquitted from all the charges.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
3. At the time of joining of the petitioner on the post of Constable(Driver) the appellant made truthful disclosure by swearing an affidavit dated 18.02.2017(Anexure-P/5) to the writ petition)
about concluded criminal case registered against him whereas he was honourably acquitted by the judgment of acquittal dated 26.09.2014.

However, the respondents by order dated 16.06.2017(Annexure-P/1 to the writ petition) rejected the candidature of the appellant on the ground that his acquittal from the criminal case is not a honourable acquittal and he was involved in an offence involving moral turpitude and, therefore, he is disqualified from being considered for appointment on the post of Constable(Driver).

Being aggrieved, the appellant preferred W.P.
No.4212/2017.
The learned Single Judge vide impugned order dated 09.02.2023 dismissed the petition.
Hence, this appeal.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the learned Single Judge erred in not appreciating the fact that the trial court while acquitting the appellant has completely disbelieved the deposition of the prosecutrix(PW1) and has held that the prosecutrix is deliberately deposing falsely to implicate the present appellant in the aforesaid crime.

The learned Single Judge instead of relying on Para-70, 71, 72, 75, 76, 83, 84, 85, 86, 87, 88 and 89 had solely relied upon Para-90 of the aforesaid judgment to hold that the acquittal of the appellant from the criminal case was not an honourable acquittal.
Para - 92 of the judgment which is an operative paragraph in which it is clearly held that the charges are not found to be proved and all the four accused persons are exonerated of the charges.

sentences.text:
Thus, in view of the law laid down by the Division Bench of this Court, in the case of State of M.P.
& Others v. Bhanu Singh Sikarwar[W.A. No.217/2017, decided on 11.10.2017(Annexure--A/4)], the appellant can by no stretch of imagination be said to be a person of "tainted antecedents"
warranting rejection of his claim for appointment on the post of Constable(Driver).
7.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent opposed the prayer by submitting that the appellant is not fit for the post of Police Constable on the ground that his acquittal is on a technical ground.
The action taken by the answering respondents is just, legal and proper.
Therefore, he prays for dismissal of the writ appeal.
8. Heard the learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.

9 . In conspectus of the above discussion and on perusal of the trial Court order acquitting the appellant, it is clear that the appellant has been acquitted honourably as per Paragraphs 90 and 92 of the judgment.
The prosecution miserably failed to even prove the genuineness of the case projected by it which relate to honourable and clean acquittal.

10. Consequently, it is obvious that while passing the impugned order dated 16.06.2017(Annexure-P/1 to the writ petition), the respondents while holding the appellant to be ineligible for appointment and thereby cancelling the candidature, failed to properly apply his mind to the aspect of acquittal being honourable, thereby rendering the impugned order dated 16.06.2017(Annexure- P/1 to the writ petition) vitiated in the eyes of law.

11. Accordingly, the present appeal is allowed to the extent indicated below :-
(i) Impugned order dated 09.02.2023, passed in W.P. No.4212/2017 is set aside.
(ii) Impugned order dated 16.6.2017(Annexure-P/1 to the writ petition), passed by the respondents is quashed for having been passed without application of mind.
